t: This was the Storran Gallery, a fashionable avant-garde art gallery of the 1930s, at 106 Brompton Road. It is no longer here, and the gallery later moved to Fitzroy Street and then to Euston Road. In 1937 it was run by the art critic Eardley Knollys, together with Ala Story and the artist Frank Coombs. Knollys belonged to the Bloomsbury Group, and worked as a critic, dealer and collector. He only began painting himself in 1949. Coombs was a painter, an architect and an art dealer, so the gallery had a practical eye as well as a critical one.
